summary: Markov-chain name generator: learns from sample names and produces new ones that sound alike.
overview: Trains a chain of character n-grams from a list of sample names, then samples it to make new ones. The results sound like the training set without ever copying one exactly. A fantasy corpus is built in so it works with no setup; supply your own list to change the flavour entirely.
useCases: NPC, town or item names that feel consistent with a setting.
Filling a large world with names without writing them all.
Re-flavouring a game by swapping the training list rather than the code.

params.tuning: How many characters of context each step sees. Low is more inventive and more nonsense; high starts reproducing the training names almost verbatim. Two or three is the usual sweet spot.
Leave empty for the built-in fantasy corpus. A small custom list (under about 20) tends to echo its inputs.
Guards against one-syllable output. Set too close to maxLength and generation can retry a lot.

gotchas.title: It can emit a training name verbatim
gotchas.body: Nothing forbids it, and a high order makes it likely. Check against the source list if names must be original.

gotchas.title: Output quality is entirely the training set
gotchas.body: A mixed corpus produces mush. Names that share a sound produce names that share a sound.
